payload.statement_nl: For integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := product_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n.

If r = 0 or r = n, then both sides are 1. Indeed, [n choose 0]_q = 1 by the given empty-product convention, and [n choose n]_q is the product over i = 1, ..., n of ((1 - q^i)/(1 - q^i)), so it is 1 as well (and if n = 0, that product is empty). Thus the claim holds in the boundary cases.

Now assume 1 <= r <= n - 1. Work in the field of rational functions in q. Set
A = [n choose r]_q,
B = [n choose n-r]_q.

By the given definition,
A = prod_{i=1}^r ((1 - q^(n-r+i))/(1 - q^i))
  = (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)).
The exponents n-r+i for i = 1, ..., r are exactly the integers n-r+1, ..., n. Therefore
A = (prod_{m=n-r+1}^n (1 - q^m)) / (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)).
Since the intervals {1, ..., n-r} and {n-r+1, ..., n} partition {1, ..., n},
prod_{m=1}^n (1 - q^m) = (prod_{m=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^m))(prod_{m=n-r+1}^n (1 - q^m)).
Hence
A = (prod_{m=1}^n (1 - q^m)) / ((prod_{m=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^m))(prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i))).

Similarly,
B = prod_{i=1}^{n-r} ((1 - q^(r+i))/(1 - q^i))
  = (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^(r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i)).
The exponents r+i for i = 1, ..., n-r are exactly the integers r+1, ..., n. So
B = (prod_{m=r+1}^n (1 - q^m)) / (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i)).
Because the intervals {1, ..., r} and {r+1, ..., n} partition {1, ..., n},
prod_{m=1}^n (1 - q^m) = (prod_{m=1}^r (1 - q^m))(prod_{m=r+1}^n (1 - q^m)).
Thus
B = (prod_{m=1}^n (1 - q^m)) / ((prod_{m=1}^r (1 - q^m))(prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i))).

The two final denominators are the same, just written with the two factors in opposite order. Therefore A = B. In other words,
[n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.
This proves the claimed symmetry.
result_payload.proof_summary: Rewrite each side as the same rational function: both [n choose r]_q and [n choose n-r]_q equal prod_{m=1}^n (1 - q^m) divided by (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i))(prod_{j=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^j)); boundary cases give 1 directly.
